title: Build an Nx-affected-backed context resolver so an agent fetches only the AGENTS.md/ADR/router-table slice relevant to a task, instead of reading broadly
objective: Continuation of MASTER-SOURCE-SPLIT-PHASE1's router table: the owner wants the context-pack concept already named in docs/architecture/ai-control-plane.md S16.9 (DEC-050) to become a real, runnable tool instead of a manual link-chase. Owner confirmed the backbone should be Nx's own affected/graph tooling (DEC-021: Nx graph export is already treated as derived structural context, zero new dependency) rather than adopting Nrwl's 'Polygraph' product, which was researched and rejected as a bad fit -- Polygraph targets cross-repository coordination and this monorepo is deliberately monolithic (DEC-045), and its cloud-backed session memory would duplicate the git-native .ai/state/tasks/ coordination system already built this session, plus trigger DEC-038/DEC-039's external-AI-integration governance for no real benefit. Owner explicitly chose automatic invocation (a PostToolUse hook firing on task claim) over a manual-only tool when asked directly via AskUserQuestion.
validations: DONE: researched the repo's real Nx setup before designing anything -- confirmed `pnpm nx show projects --affected --files=<paths> --json` works today and correctly expands direct hits into real downstream dependents (verified: packages/ui/src/index.ts -> ["ui","architecture-studio","grafting"]), and that docs/generated/project-graph.json already contains every project's root in one file (node.data.root), avoiding N per-project `nx show project --json` calls.

DONE: ran a Plan-Mode design pass (approved by the owner) covering: primary input mode (task ID reading its own affected_paths per DEC-031, not a new git-diff convention), ADR matching strategy (DEC-XXX/GATE-XXX id matching against docs/adr/README.md's index table, not fuzzy keyword search over free-text Subject prose -- confirmed via research that no structured tag column exists), and script placement (Node under tools/scripts/, matching where every other doc/graph tool already lives, not Python).
DONE: asked the owner directly (AskUserQuestion) whether invocation should be manual-only or automatic; owner chose automatic via a PostToolUse hook.

DONE: wrote tools/scripts/context-resolver.mjs -- pure functions (parseProjectGraphRoots, matchDirectProjects, parseRouterTable, matchRouterRows, parseAdrIndexTable, matchAdrRows, resolveAgentsFiles, extractDecGateIds, formatContextDigest) plus one injectable impure boundary (runNxAffected, defaults to execFileSync but accepts a fake exec for tests) plus a thin CLI (--task <ID> | --paths a,b [--root <path>]), following doc-size.mjs/check-doc-organization.mjs's established pure-functions-plus-thin-CLI split and doc-size-reminder.mjs's manual --flag value parsing (no new dependency). 22 new node --test cases, all passing, including a real Windows path-separator bug caught and fixed in the test fixture itself (a fake `exists` predicate compared forward-slash strings against `path.resolve`'s native-separator output).

DONE: wrote tools/scripts/context-resolver-hook.mjs -- a PostToolUse reminder (matching research-registry-reminder.mjs/doc-size-reminder.mjs/third-party-attribution-reminder.mjs's exact advisory shape: reads hook JSON from stdin, never blocks, never throws) that fires when a Write/Edit leaves a `.ai/state/tasks/<status>/<ID>.json` record (matched via the same path shape as agent-task-guard.mjs's own TASK_RECORD regex) at status in_progress, reading the file fresh from disk rather than trusting tool_input (Edit's input is only a diff). Reuses context-resolver.mjs's resolveContext directly -- no duplicated logic between the manual CLI and the hook. 7 new node --test cases (tmp-dir-isolated, real files on disk for the task record, an injectable fake resolver for the resolveContext call), all passing.

DONE: wired context-resolver-hook.mjs into .claude/settings.json's PostToolUse hooks (same Write|Edit matcher as the other three reminders), with a 30s timeout (vs the others' 10s) since it may shell out to the real Nx CLI.

DONE: ran two real smoke tests (not just unit tests) against actual repository state: `--task CONTEXT-RESOLVER-NX-BACKED` (this task's own broad affected_paths, including nx.json/root AGENTS.md/a whole tools/scripts/ directory, correctly and honestly caused Nx to mark nearly the whole workspace as affected -- a real, documented limitation, not a bug: root-level/global-file changes legitimately affect everything in Nx's own model) and `--paths packages/ui/src/molecules/preview-card.tsx` (a realistic narrow case, correctly resolved to exactly 3 AGENTS.md files: root, packages/ui, and apps/architecture-studio as the real downstream consumer -- confirming the tool is genuinely selective for typical tasks, not just for this task's own atypically-broad one).

DONE: documented both new scripts in tools/scripts/README.md (including the root-level-affected-paths limitation, stated plainly) and added a short, non-mandatory mention to .ai/coordination/PROTOCOL.md's 'Starting work' section (the hook fires automatically on claim per DEC-029's progressive-disclosure principle; explicitly framed as 'a starting point, not a substitute for judgment').

DONE: ran the full node --test tools/scripts/*.test.mjs (107 tests: 94 pass, 13 fail) and `uv run --package automation pytest` (7/7 pass) suites. The 13 failures are the exact same pre-existing, already-documented-in-prior-tasks set (11 agent-task-guard.test.mjs fixture-path issues, 1 generate-domain.test.mjs environmental, 1 graph-ir-extract.test.mjs latent regression) -- confirmed unrelated to and unworsened by this task's own new files. `node tools/scripts/check-doc-organization.mjs` output unchanged from before this task (4 documents flagged, 1 colossal, same as after MASTER-SOURCE-SPLIT-PHASE1).
artifacts: tools/scripts/README.md (documents both new scripts, including the root-level-affected-paths limitation)
risks: A task whose affected_paths includes root-level/global files (nx.json, root AGENTS.md, a whole directory like tools/scripts/) will make Nx's --affected computation legitimately mark most or all of the workspace as affected -- correct per Nx's own dependency model, but not a sharp per-task signal in that case. Documented plainly in tools/scripts/README.md rather than papered over with a heuristic 'ignore broad paths' filter, which would risk hiding a genuinely global impact.

The context-resolver-hook re-fires its digest on every subsequent Write/Edit to an already-in_progress task record (e.g. mid-task validations/artifacts updates), not only on the initial claim, since it checks current resulting state rather than a before/after diff -- an explicit, accepted tradeoff matching doc-size-reminder.mjs's own existing precedent, not a new gap invented here.

docs/generated/project-graph.json is read as-is, not regenerated on each resolver run -- if it drifts stale relative to the real Nx graph, the resolved project-root mapping could be stale too. Not solved in this pass; the existing generate-graph-ir.mjs --check freshness mechanism is the appropriate place to catch this, not the resolver itself.

ADR matching is id-based only (DEC-XXX/GATE-XXX mentioned in a task's own title/objective) since docs/adr/README.md's index table has no structured tag column -- a task that's relevant to an ADR without citing its DEC/GATE id anywhere in its own text will not surface that ADR. Router-table matching is a plain case-insensitive substring match on topic text, which is a cheap heuristic (some false negatives on paraphrased topics, occasional harmless false positives), not an authoritative index.
None of this session's uncommitted changes (this task's or prior tasks') have been committed or pushed.
